title: Browser sizing contexts
contract: Dragging Browser dividers resizes panels; dragging its bottom edge closes Info and the active Clip/Device View. Full-Height Browser instead expands while those views remain open. Geometry limits and focus restoration remain U.

title: Content columns and sorting entrypoints
contract: Name is always shown; Content Options offers extra columns and file-extension visibility. Headers can be reordered and clicked for ascending/descending sorting. Sort keys, Unicode comparison, missing values and ties remain U.

title: Tag-query entry and suggestions
contract: Typing # followed by a tag name exposes tag auto-complete suggestions. Ordinary word matching/clear/global-find behavior stays with Browser Workflows001..004; tag parser, matching, suggestion ranking and boolean algebra remain U.

title: Custom result-label editing
contract: Add Label saves a search/filter result label in Library. Its context menu removes a custom label; factory/custom labels offer rename and icon choice. Dynamic versus snapshot membership and durable storage are not established.

title: Per-label filter presentation
contract: Filter View can be shown/hidden, with label-specific groups shown through its menu or hidden by group context. Enabled filter state is recalled between Library labels; Ctrl Windows/Cmd Mac permits multiple tags in a group. Reset Filter Groups to Default restores visible groups, not a new search algebra.

title: Factory tag edit restrictions
contract: The chapter distinguishes factory/default tags and groups from user additions: factory-item default tags and default groups/tags cannot be removed or edited, while added user tags are allowed. Exact permissions, error presentation and serialization stay U or with Browser Index.

title: Automatic analysis and plug-in metadata tags
contract: Current documentation describes periodic sound analysis assigning a best-matching tag to user samples up to60 seconds, and VST3 metadata tags when a subcategory maps to a Live category. Analysis timing, duration-boundary admission, classification/model, category mapping and accuracy remain U; native index fields provide no algorithm.

title: Auto Tags controls
contract: Enable Auto Tags is offered in Filter View. Tag Editor can remove auto tags or change them to user tags. Source provenance conversion, future rescans, durability and classification remain U.

title: Tag Editor assignment and custom creation
contract: Filter View opens Tag Editor; it shows selected-item tags, foldable groups and assigned-group emphasis. Checkbox edits can tag one or Shift-selected multiple files; Add Tag and Add Group create custom entries, with a group exposed in Filter View after one of its tags is assigned.

title: Nested and custom tag editing
contract: Add Subtag in creates a nested tag under a parent; Creator-group tags do not permit subtags. Parent tags fold/unfold; custom tags/groups offer rename/delete. Editor closes through X or its Filter View entry; default-item restrictions remain separate.

title: Quick Tags creation
contract: Quick Tags Add offers existing-tag auto-complete or Create new tag followed by parent/group selection. An unrecognized parent/group name offers creation of a parent tag or group. No arbitrary nesting, collision or text grammar is specified.

title: Quick Tags selection presentation
contract: Quick Tags shows assigned tags, with additions described in alphabetical order. Multi-selection shows the union and marks nonshared tags with an asterisk; selecting a tag shows its group in Status Bar. X removes user assignments, and Filter View can hide the section. Exact collation and saved visibility remain U.

title: Collection assignment entrypoints
contract: Selected items, including mixed types/folders or multiple items, can receive Collections colors through context or keys1..7;0 resets assignments. This is Browser-focused UI assignment, not a global shortcut or new sidecar color encoding. Existing collection-membership and sidecar owners remain authoritative.

title: Collection item presentation
contract: Collection folders can unfold. Content-pane color icons represent assignments, with at most three displayed even when an item has more colors. Collection membership itself remains Browser Workflows006; no color palette or chosen-color truncation order is established.

title: Collection label name and visibility
contract: Collection labels support context rename or Browser-focused Ctrl/Cmd-R, and header Edit exposes Show/Hide Label with Done. Assigning a hidden previously unassigned color reveals its label; removing all assignments does not automatically hide a visible label.

title: Library label presentation
contract: Library presents type-oriented labels and header Edit/Done visibility selection. Their described contents are discovery roles, not a new extension-kind, plug-in admission, ranking or index algorithm. Source-described default visibility is not exact-target observation.

title: Places content entry roles
contract: Places exposes configured Packs, Splice, Cloud, Push, User Library, Current Project and user-folder entrypoints. Its actual labels depend on configuration; settings-owned Show Splice/Cloud/Push controls do not prove available services or hardware.

title: Installed Pack presentation
contract: Installed Packs appear as expandable folders under Packs, with their presets/samples/Live Clips also exposed in appropriate Library labels. This is a known installed-catalog view, not an ALP codec, install transaction or universal content-admission law.

title: Pack updates and available catalog
contract: Packs Updates exposes available updates for installed Packs; Available Packs exposes owned uninstalled Packs. Ownership/catalog validity, refresh ordering, stale state and entitlement protocol remain U.

title: Pack download controls
contract: The source describes download/progress, pause/resume/cancel and corresponding context commands, including selected multiple Packs. These are workflow roles only; bytes, authentication, queue order, retry, progress scale, cancellation and partial-file outcomes remain U.

title: Pack install and delete roles
contract: After download the source offers Install with a progress dialog. Installed Pack context/Delete removes it and makes it available again. This is distinct from project-Pack creation/restore under Project Media021; atomicity, dependencies, rights, deletion extent and service refresh remain U.

title: Pack size and downloadable visibility
contract: Content Options can expose Pack size in Updates/Available Packs. Library settings Show Downloadable Packs hides/shows those sections. Size units/accuracy, capacity prediction and default visibility are not new numerical laws.

title: Pack Info entrypoints
contract: Installed Packs can expose Show Pack Info, and Help Pack Overview opens installed Pack Info pages. Content may include creator/summary/tutorial; the Core Library is documented without a Pack Info page. No external tutorial or content decoder is specified.

title: Splice Home and connection prerequisite
contract: The Splice label Home exposes navigation/search, Search with Sound and category entrypoints, with login/signup entries. Viewing its content requires an active Internet connection. Settings-owned label visibility and account/service availability remain distinct.

title: Splice device-confirmation login role
contract: Login/Try free opens an OS browser for Splice device confirmation and then account entry; the source describes matching confirmation codes in browser and Live. This supplies no credential, token, code-generation, security, entitlement or login-success law.

title: Splice account-dependent capabilities
contract: The source distinguishes unauthenticated browse/preview from logged-in Set insertion, library saving and Search with Sound. Logged-in Home exposes Library and rearranged browse/search areas. Free/paid catalog contents, counts, rights and subscription behavior remain unknown.

title: Splice search and result controls
contract: Splice has its own category/query suggestions, Samples/Packs view, tag/filter expansion and sorting options including Random/shuffle. Selected category scopes subsequent text search. Exact result matching, ranking, RNG, counts and history retention remain U; native Browser matching is not borrowed.

title: Splice Search with Sound
contract: Logged-in Search with Sound accepts a dragged clip or captured time selection; the source describes compatible results and reference replay/replacement/removal. Its reported50-result list is source context, not a target count or quality oracle. Model, upload, scoring, rights and rendering remain U.

title: Splice sample-row entrypoints
contract: Sample rows expose pack navigation, sample-type/name/tags and context actions for Likes/Collections or pack view. Hover/selection can expose Like and expanded pane shows Time/Key/BPM columns. Display metadata does not establish audio analysis, source type or stored service identity.

title: Splice preview settings
contract: Splice preview has its own play/name entry, loop/timestretch/original-tempo, selected-key/Live-scale and loudness options. Source defaults and preview synchronization supply no waveform, gain, pitch, scale, render or timing law; native Browser Preview remains a separate owner.

title: Splice import Warp context
contract: Splice samples have service-specific drag/double-click/Enter/device destinations. The source describes Complex Warp overriding the ordinary default for clips using Splice samples; this is unverified source context, not a new Warp algorithm, decode result or guaranteed preview identity.

title: Splice sample registration and location
contract: The source describes Set insertion as licensing/registering a sample in the Splice library and storing downloads under User Library/Samples/Splice, Current Project/Samples/Splice or Custom Folder. These are source workflow/location roles, not a legal-rights conclusion, default-build promise, file transaction or service codec.

title: Splice Library and Collections controls
contract: Splice Library presents Likes, Collections and previously loaded/downloaded samples. Its Collections page/menu offers creation, name/description edit, private/share-link and delete controls. This is separate from Browser color Collections; publication, privacy enforcement and saved server state remain U.

title: Splice Settings information routes
contract: Splice Settings offers subscription/display, usage-log download, certified-license information, Knowledge Base/feedback and logged-out Login entrypoints. No subscription, usage-log format, legal validity, support service or credential behavior is specified.

title: Ableton Cloud authorization entry
contract: Cloud label offers a Sign In browser route to authorize Ableton Cloud, after which synced Move/Note Sets appear. The published up-to-eight Set description is source context, not an exact-target quota, sync protocol, account entitlement or version-compatibility promise.

title: Cloud assets and direction boundary
contract: Synced Set assets require an accessible User Library; ABL Assets stores Move/Note assets. The chapter describes Move/Note-to-Live sync rather than Live-to-source and recommends Collect All and Save for developed Sets. Existing project/media collection and missing-reference owners retain their laws.

title: Push3 standalone pairing entry
contract: Browser Push transfer requires Push3 Standalone and the same Wi-Fi network. Named-device selection/Connect precedes a code displayed on Push and entered in Live. The six-digit description is not a wire or pairing-code algorithm; Push1/2/controller mode cannot substitute.

title: Paired Push file-view controls
contract: After successful pairing, saved Standalone Project folders and Push User Library appear. Switching away/back refreshes the list; Push-label Disconnect unpairs. These are Browser file-view entrypoints, not file-transfer integrity, discovery timing or Push3 standalone/controller compatibility.

title: Push continuity prerequisites
contract: The chapter describes Standalone Set transfer/open on computer and transfer back using native devices, frozen plug-in tracks and collected Project samples. These are prerequisites/guidance, not an arbitrary Set/device codec, plugin parity, successful transfer or full Push3 contract.

title: User Library folder entry roles
contract: User Library exposes user-saved content and custom folders; source folder roles include ABL Assets, Chord Banks, Clips, Defaults, Grooves, Presets, Samples and Templates. Existing owners retain save/default/Stacks/groove/media/template and dependent-copy semantics; folder names do not establish codecs or constructor contents.

title: User Library manager and Project reveal
contract: File Manage Files then Manage User Library opens that Library overview; Current Project context Show in Explorer/Finder reveals its folder. Project Media retains Set file management and reference operations, and Settings retains location selection.

title: Current Project Backup presentation
contract: The chapter describes a Backup folder after repeated saves, timestamped prior Sets and bounded retention with old backups moved to trash; unsaved Sets use a temporary Project without Backup. Its twice-saved/last-ten wording remains source context, not a new recovery, retention-timing, filesystem or restore law.

title: Folder scan, locate and removal entrypoints
contract: A Places scan has a spinning progress indicator. For a registered folder, Locate Folder and Remove from Sidebar are offered; removal also applies to an available folder. Existing Browser Workflows007/008 owns nonrelocating registration and dimmed unavailable entries; retry/index timing and deletion effects remain U.

title: Multi-folder expansion modifier
contract: Opening another folder normally closes previously open folders; Ctrl Windows/Cmd Mac while opening overrides that behavior. Generic arrows/focus remain Keyboard Navigation-owned; selection, layout/IME, hidden folders and persistence require their own contexts.

title: Native preview Raw and scrubbing context
contract: Beyond existing generic preview, the chapter describes waveform scrubbing except unwarped saved clips, Raw original-tempo/unlooped versus non-Raw next-bar/looped preview, and no scrubbing in Raw. Cue/routing owns output selection; all sound, loop, onset and tempo algorithms remain U.

title: Explicit preview gesture without toggle
contract: Shift-Enter or right arrow on a selected eligible Browser item can request preview even with Preview toggle off. Existing Browser Workflows009 owns generic preview; focus conflict, actual sound and cancellation/timing remain U.

title: Browser Similarity Search entry
contract: Compatible selected Browser files offer Show Similar Files icon/context and Ctrl-Shift-F Windows/Cmd-Shift-F Mac entry. This owns Browser entrypoints only; Clip View042 retains its corresponding entry and sample-file management.

title: Similarity source and ranking role
contract: Concepts describes comparing a reference against Core/User Library samples up to60 seconds, instrument/drum presets, then listing results from most to least similar. Similar Sample Swapping names Drum Rack, Simpler and Drum Sampler targets. No embedding/model, scoring, threshold, exact result/order, boundary admission or replacement algorithm is supplied.

title: Similarity background-analysis status
contract: The Concepts source says similarity needs analysis, with new-user-file background work reported in Status Bar and a Pause control; Core Library is described as pre-analyzed. This clause owns status/Pause affordances, not a scan trigger, completion deadline, resume law, index lifecycle or generated features.

title: Similarity custom-label reference presentation
contract: For a custom User Label saved from Similarity Search results, the reference sound is shown at the top. General custom-label editing stays above; reference identity is distinct from any numerical similarity rank or successful sample replacement.

title: Query, tags and result algebra
contract: Tag/query grammar, boolean combination, collation/Unicode/IME, hierarchy/sort ties, filter counts, dynamic label refresh and index-to-UI result identity remain unknown.

title: Automatic classification and similarity algorithms
contract: Sound-analysis eligibility,60-second boundaries, models/features/scoring, periodic scheduling, CPU behavior, rankings/thresholds/RNG and swap sound/state outcomes remain unknown.

title: Accounts, catalogs and legal/service boundaries
contract: Online capability, credentials/tokens/device confirmation, free/paid entitlements/catalogs/quotas, sample rights, logs/licenses, privacy/sharing, availability and server protocols remain unknown. No legal interpretation follows from marketing or registration prose.

title: Cloud and Push file identity
contract: Cloud/Push versions, pairing/discovery, permissions, codecs, dependency/device portability, synchronization/conflict order, partial copies and direction/capacity limits remain unknown; no Push3 standalone or controller profile is completed.

title: Content transactions and saved state
contract: Pack install/update/delete, Library reconfiguration, backup retention, downloads/paths/collisions, tagging side effects, Undo/cancel, saved browser state and migration remain unknown beyond existing finite owners.

title: Input admission and cross-cutting lifecycle
contract: Malformed/unavailable content, focus/preferences, unsupported controls, transport/automation/rate changes, source loss, concurrency and teardown retain null outcomes; missing capability or positive input is never a negative pass.
